prompt: Walk through this NestJS + Jest integration test setup with me: the suite passes every single time when run serially, but once CI lets Jest fan the spec files out across its default parallel workers, a handful of tests fail — and the SET of failing tests changes from run to run. The failures are always the same shape: a test creates a row, then asserts a count or a row's fields, and instead sees 0 rows or an unexpected extra row. Here's the jest config, the shared test-database setup, and one representative failing spec. Diagnose why this only breaks under parallelism — don't just rewrite the assertions — name the two structural fixes, and tell me how you'd prove your diagnosis and stop it from regressing.
